newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close lower as soybeans falter.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close lower as soybeans falter.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed lower on a weather and technical break in soybeans, traders said.
Friday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for above normal temperatures in the U.S. Midwest from September 19 through September 23.
The market has been on edge amid concerns about an early frost since much of the U.S. soybean crop was planted late and needs more time to develop and mature.
Chilly weather over the weekend in the Midwest failed to generate buying interest.
Agronomists said some damage was noted in a frost Saturday in portions of southern Minnesota and northern Iowa.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, up from 12,865 Friday, according to the CBOT. Soyoil options volume was estimated at 2,800 contracts, up from 986 Friday.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, down from 21,016 Friday. Soymeal options volume was estimated at 1,800 contracts, down from 3,347 Friday.
Soyoil futures closed 0.25 to 0.41 cent per lb lower, with September down 0.38 at 25.27 cents. Soymeal was $0.90 to $2.30 per ton lower, with September down $0.90 at $271.30.
